name: Academic Elite
value: Seven awards: four years of tuition, first-year standard housing, and $9,000/year for four years. One top award: tuition, first-year housing, $9,000 in year one, $19,000/year in years two through four, plus a $5,000 research/study allowance.
deadline: December 8, 2026, 11:59 p.m. Central (Witt Fellows application and any endorsement)
apply: Obtain UA admission and submit Honors College and Witt Fellows applications, including anonymous resume and essays, by December 8, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Central. Any required endorsement form has the same deadline. Semifinalists interview in late January 2027; finalists attend February 19-20, 2027 interviews. Eight Witt Fellows receive Academic Elite.
eligibility: Admitted first-time freshmen applying to Witt Fellows: automatic route requires at least 3.5 high-school GPA and non-superscored ACT 32 or SAT 1420. Applicants outside those thresholds may use an endorsement from a high-school representative or UA faculty member with at least non-superscored ACT 29 or SAT 1330. Honors College acceptance is required.
notes: Maintain Witt Fellows membership for four-year funding; program requirements include overall 3.5 GPA, the 16-credit Social Innovation and Leadership minor and required Black Belt experience. Academic Elite replaces a lower-value previous UA merit package; National Merit stipends reduce its supplemental award. Institutional funds are capped at cost of attendance. Top-award $5,000 research/international-study allowance is available after one year at UA. Housing covers the regular room rate only in year one.

name: MAPS
value: Tuition, fees, room and board; twelve awards annually.
deadline: January 15 (displayed without a year)
apply: Submit the scholarship application, resume and two recommendations; selected applicants interview.
eligibility: Minimum 3.5 high-school GPA and ACT 30 or SAT 1360. Renewal requires 3.25 college GPA and full-time enrollment.
notes: MAPS-specific criteria remain 3.5 high-school GPA and ACT 30/SAT 1360 despite a general test-optional statement on the page. Renewal requires 3.25 UM cumulative GPA and full-time enrollment of 12 hours per semester; MAPS-specific maximum duration is not stated. The page lists MAPS among scholarships that cannot be held together, and institutional awards cannot exceed direct cost of attendance. The January 15 application date has no year.

name: Hays Memorial Scholarship
value: Tuition, fees, room and board (confirmed for the Class of 2029 cohort, four recipients).
deadline: 2027 scholarship deadline not verified
apply: Recent cohort selection used an essay and group interviews. Current application details not yet published.
eligibility: The confirmed Class of 2029 selection included U.S. and international applicants with outstanding academic achievement. Current 2027 eligibility thresholds are not confirmed.
notes: The June 2025 Class of 2029 announcement confirms four recipients and direct-cost coverage that rises with tuition. The current financial-aid directory does not publish detailed Hays terms. Current award duration, renewal and 2027 application instructions remain unconfirmed; general admission dates do not establish a Hays deadline.

name: First-year academic merit (Trustee Scholars unconfirmed)
value: Automatic first-year academic merit consideration; awards can continue for up to four years or eight semesters. Current dollar amounts and an active Trustee full-ride program are not published in the material reviewed.
deadline: No current Trustee-specific deadline verified
apply: Apply for first-year admission; LMU automatically considers all admission applicants for academic merit. Accept admission, pay the tuition deposit and accept an offered scholarship through PROWL.
eligibility: All incoming first-year applicants receive merit consideration regardless of citizenship, unless specific scholarship guidelines say otherwise. Full-time enrollment of at least 12 units is required.
notes: Presidential and most listed merit awards require 3.0 cumulative GPA; Leavey Family Foundation and University Hill Foundation require 3.2. Funding ends at the first bachelor’s degree or eight semesters and excludes summer and non-LMU study abroad. Other aid may reduce awards. A current Trustee award and published award amounts remain unconfirmed.

name: Merit awards (Trustee, Presidential, Mork)
value: Merit awards up to full tuition. Presidential is half tuition. Current Mork award count and package unresolved.
deadline: November 1, 2026 (EA/ED) for Dornsife merit consideration; audition-based schools can differ
apply: Submit the admission application by the relevant school’s merit deadline. No separate need-based aid application is required for Office of Admission merit consideration. Current Mork-specific selection instructions are not published in reviewed material.
eligibility: Admission applicants by the merit deadline.
notes: The 2026-27 guide covers Trustee, Presidential and other admission merit awards for eight semesters, or ten for the five-year Bachelor of Architecture, subject to full-time enrollment, academic standing, annual progress ordinarily 30 units and conduct standards. Awards are mutually exclusive; other tuition funding and total cost-of-attendance limits can reduce awards. Mork availability and package remain unconfirmed. The fall 2027 first-year page confirms performing-arts applicants use December 1 Regular Decision for merit consideration; Dornsife confirms November 1, 2026 EA/ED.

name: Eugene du Pont Memorial Distinguished Scholar
value: Four years of tuition, standard on-campus room/board, health/student-center fees; $625 each fall and spring for books; one-time $5,000 enrichment grant.
deadline: November 1 Early Action (displayed without a year)
apply: Apply EA for Honors consideration. Top admitted Honors applicants are invited to compete and interview.
eligibility: No fixed SAT/GPA minimum published. Invitation only.
notes: No public self-application to du Pont; selected admitted Honors applicants are invited to interview. General university aid requires full-time enrollment of 12 earned credits, with prorating for eligible graduating seniors, and an eight-semester maximum. Specific du Pont GPA and renewal criteria are not publicly stated in the pages reviewed. General November 1 Honors deadline has no explicit cycle year.

name: Archdiocesan Scholarship
value: Full tuition for up to four years or eight semesters of full-time undergraduate study, ending at the first degree.
deadline: Nomination notices mid-December; no scholarship application cutoff published
apply: No separate scholarship application. Selection on academics, rigor, leadership and an invited interview.
eligibility: Religious eligibility needs clarification: university policy distinguishes Archdiocesan from a Trustee award whose recipients need not be Roman Catholic.
notes: Renewal requires continuous full-time enrollment of at least 12 credits, satisfactory academic progress and 3.20 cumulative GPA. The policy distinguishes Trustee awards as not requiring Roman Catholic affiliation; current Archdiocesan religious eligibility remains unclear. General scholarship consideration requires a timely admission application; no cycle-specific cutoff is published on the scholarship page.

name: Howard University Freshman Scholarships (HUFS)
value: HUFS includes Presidential, Achievers, Founders, Capstone, Leadership, Opportunity and Access awards; only one HUFS type may be received. Awards may be merit-based or need-based and can renew for up to eight consecutive undergraduate semesters or graduation. Amounts and tier thresholds are not published.
deadline: EA/ED November 1, 2026; RD February 1, 2027
apply: Automatic consideration; no separate application. Domestic applicants submit FAFSA; international applicants ISFAA.
eligibility: Incoming first-time-in-college fall applicants, including international and test-optional applicants. Domestic applicants need a FAFSA; international and DACA applicants use ISFAA. Merit considers academic records and optional tests; need-based tiers consider Student Aid Index.
notes: Current admission page is for fall 2027 and requires FAFSA/ISFAA by the applicable application deadline for priority consideration. Accept the HUFS contract in Bison Hub and sign/submit its acceptance agreement by the individually designated deadline. Full-time earned-credit and GPA renewal requirements are specified in individual contracts rather than public tier tables.

name: Alfond Scholars
value: Tuition, fees, a double room and a 15-swipe meal plan for eight full-time fall/spring semesters. Books, health insurance, personal expenses and taxes are excluded. The published $83,570 annual estimate is for 2026-27. Federal/state awards count toward the package.
deadline: November 15 EA or ED I (displayed without a year)
apply: Submit complete EA or ED I admission application by the undated November 15 deadline, including transcript, application essay, recommendation and activities. International applicants also submit English proficiency and Non-U.S. Citizen Financial Aid Application. Selected finalists have virtual interviews.
eligibility: Fall first-time college applicants, including international and test-optional students; spring and transfer applicants are excluded. At most two completed gap years. The academic page lists GPA higher than 3.9 for test-optional Alfond consideration; other quoted score/GPA figures are typical competitive profiles rather than universal floors.
notes: Renewal requires 3.33 GPA and 24 completed credits annually. Scholars must live on campus four years, complete Honors, first-year Intersession Service Immersion and an off-campus experience within the first three years. Main page says up to 10 recipients and February/March interviews/results; FAQ says 10-12 and January/February stages. Confirm cycle-specific timeline.

name: Stamps and other premier merit awards
value: Stamps covers full cost of attendance, including tuition/fees, on-campus housing, meal plan, university health insurance, textbooks, laptop allowance and a $12,000 enrichment fund requiring advance approval. Singer, Weeks and Hammond cover full tuition. Awards last up to eight semesters, or ten for eligible five-year programs, ending at the first degree.
deadline: Premier consideration requires EA or ED I admission application by November 1; the program pages do not state a cycle year. Optional Hammond nomination opens September 1 and closes November 13, also undated.
apply: Apply and be admitted through EA or ED I; no separate initial premier application. Stamps semifinalists interview with the university committee, then finalists with the Stamps Foundation; recipients announced early March. Singer, Weeks and Hammond announce with EA decisions in late January. Hammond nomination is optional.
eligibility: Incoming first-year students selected through holistic review. Stamps and Singer consider all citizenships; Weeks and Hammond require U.S. citizenship or permanent residence. Renewal requires at least 12 credits each fall/spring, 24 per academic year and 3.0 GPA for the academic year, initially measured after the second semester.
notes: Current university pages replace the inaccessible old Stamps URL and outdated sponsor thresholds. Only one admission merit scholarship may be received. Other grants, scholarship/prepaid tuition or housing aid may revise awards, and total student aid cannot exceed cost of attendance. Stamps here differs from Frost School of Music Stamps. The four programs have different coverage/citizenship rules; no fixed current SAT/ACT floor is stated.

name: Marvin B. Perry Presidential
value: Full tuition, housing and dining for up to four years.
deadline: Apply by January 15 EA II; essay by February 6 (displayed without a year, not confirmed for 2027)
apply: Top first-year applicants are invited to compete.
eligibility: Must satisfy Agnes Scott's admission policy (a college centered on undergraduate education for women).
notes: Top first-year applicants are invited through the admission letter and must submit a Presidential essay. The scholarship section still shows an undated February 6 extension; the page’s separate $100K+ Promise explicitly covers fall 2027 but does not date the Presidential extension. General merit renewal requires satisfactory academic progress and the scholarship-specific conditions in the admission letter; Presidential-specific renewal thresholds are not public.

name: Robert W. Woodruff Scholarship
value: Full tuition, required fees, on-campus housing and meals for up to eight regular fall/spring undergraduate semesters, with application-based summer, research, internship and travel funding opportunities.
deadline: November 1 (ED I); November 15 (ED II/RD scholarship consideration)
apply: Submit admission materials and answer YES to the Scholars question. Finalists undergo further selection.
eligibility: Incoming Emory College first-year applicants, including international and homeschooled applicants regardless of citizenship, showing promise in the Scholars Qualities. No fixed scholarship SAT/GPA cutoff is published.
notes: Answer Yes to Scholars consideration; otherwise the applicant is not considered. Finalists located in the U.S. must attend the multi-day spring campus visit and interviews, at university expense. Renewal requires high personal/academic standards and semester/annual program requirements provided upon acceptance; the Emory College-specific numerical renewal GPA is not published on these pages. Oxford’s separately published GPA should not be applied to this Emory College award.

name: Stamps President's Scholars
value: Tuition, mandatory fees, housing, meals, books/supplies, personal allowance and laptop stipend, plus $12,000 enrichment.
deadline: Georgia applicants: October 15, 2026 EA I; documents October 30 and scores November 16. Non-Georgia applicants: November 2, 2026 EA II; documents November 16 and scores December 8. Deadlines are 11:59 p.m. in the applicant’s time zone. Semifinalist interviews early February 2027; required finalist weekend April 9-10, 2027. A linked Gold Scholars page instead lists November 3, 2026 for EA II; use the earlier admission deadline and confirm the discrepancy.
apply: Apply through the relevant Georgia Tech Early Action plan; no separate initial scholarship application. Selected semifinalists complete asynchronous virtual interviews and finalists must attend all weekend activities.
eligibility: New first-year students who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents or UK citizens; citizens of the Republic of Ireland may also be considered. Transfers are excluded. No definite SAT/ACT, GPA or class-rank cutoff is published.
notes: Four-year program includes a $1,100 laptop stipend and $12,000 enrichment fund. Georgia residents’ packages include expected HOPE/Zell Miller support; nonresidents receive an in-state tuition waiver. General aid rules limit institutional awards to eight full-time terms, ordinarily two funded semesters annually, but Stamps-specific renewal GPA is not public. The dated program calendar says early February interviews and April 9-10, 2027 weekend; the undated FAQ still says late January and mid-March. One combined Stamps President’s award, not two separate awards.

name: 1906 Scholars
value: Full tuition for up to eight semesters. Treatment of the nonresident tuition differential is not explained.
deadline: January 15, 2027 (Honors scholarship priority); interviews February 12 or 19, 2027
apply: Complete university admission and the separate Honors College application.
eligibility: Incoming fall freshmen admitted to Georgia Southern and applying to Honors; all undergraduate majors considered. Honors admission uses holistic review with no minimum score requirement. Renewal depends on good standing in Honors.
notes: Submit the Honors application by January 15, 2027 and be admitted to Georgia Southern for consideration; selected applicants interview February 12 or 19, 2027. Honors curriculum for fall 2024 entrants onward requires 3.3 cumulative Georgia Southern GPA, 18 Honors credits with at least 3 per semester until complete and experiential activities in four categories. The source does not explain nonresident tuition differential coverage. Honors scholarships can combine with HOPE/Zell Miller to cover other costs.

name: Foundation Fellowship
value: Annual stipends vary by residency. The financial-aid chart for 2026-27 lists $15,750 in-state, $25,930 out-of-state and $30,000 international, with a full nonresident/international tuition-differential waiver where applicable. The Honors page lists lower figures of $15,050, $25,900 and $28,800. Travel benefits include three group spring trips, first-year Oxford study abroad, up to $10,000 individual travel grants and up to $2,000 research/conference grants. Confirm 2027 amounts.
deadline: UGA Early Action October 15; Honors/Foundation Fellowship application November 1 (recurring dates)
apply: Apply EA, then complete the Honors application and embedded Fellowship section, including the biographical statement/video.
eligibility: Incoming first-year students not previously matriculated at another university, including dual-enrolled high-school seniors and international applicants; transfers and current undergraduates excluded from the entering-student award. Financial-aid page says international academic-scholarship applicants must hold F-1 visas; confirm applicability to the Fellowship. No fixed current test minimum is published.
notes: Renewal requires 3.40 cumulative UGA GPA, at least 12 semester hours except summer, good Honors standing, program events/travel reports/community participation and graduation in four years; first-year Myers Hall residence required. Financial aid limits awards to eight full-time semesters or first degree, with one approved part-time exception. Ramsey merged with Fellowship in 2021. Program application page still dates mandatory interviews February 20-21, 2026, so 2027 interview dates are unconfirmed.

name: Automatic academic merit (Presidential unconfirmed)
value: Automatic first-year academic merit: $44,000-$50,000 annually. The separate Rothwell Stephens mathematics scholarship provides $5,000 annually. Awards apply to tuition and renew with good academic standing; maximum duration is not published.
deadline: General merit is considered with admission. Rothwell Stephens: admission application and mathematics examination by January 15 (year unstated); March 15 notification. Fall 2027 dates are unconfirmed.
apply: Apply for admission for automatic academic merit. For Rothwell Stephens, request and take the mathematics examination on campus or under a high-school mathematics teacher’s supervision.
eligibility: Admitted first-year students are considered for academic merit, including international applicants. Rothwell Stephens is for an incoming first-year student interested in mathematics with an outstanding examination score; continued mathematics interest is required.
notes: Current automatic merit and mathematics awards are confirmed; the older full-tuition Presidential award is not. International applicants must document funding, and ability to pay can affect admission. Knox scholarships/grants plus federal/state grants cannot exceed tuition.

name: Duchossois Leadership Scholars
value: Full undergraduate tuition for up to four years, with possible petition for a fifth year; four years of double-occupancy campus housing and full meal coverage, including registered summer sessions. Funded summer experience, retreats and mentoring; books, fees and computers are not covered.
deadline: November 15 admission, scholarship application and recommendations (year unstated). January finalist notification; February campus interview; April 1 scholarship acceptance and May 1 enrollment confirmation (years unstated). Fall 2027 dates are unconfirmed.
apply: Apply Early Action or Early Decision through Common App and submit the scholarship application, 500-word leadership/service essay, résumé and two recommendations by November 15. Counselor nomination is optional. Finalists interview on campus.
eligibility: Incoming first-year U.S. citizens or permanent residents, any major, with at least a 3.5 high-school GPA, exceptional academics and leadership/service. Household adjusted gross income must be below $300,000; currently enrolled students are ineligible.
notes: Live on campus for the first two years; later off-campus living loses housing/meal support. Maintain 3.25 GPA: two consecutive semesters below it terminate eligibility. Program participation, semester grade sharing and annual foundation report are required, with a letter of intent for $100 annual donations after graduation. Other Illinois Tech institutional scholarships do not stack; MAP coordination caps combined restricted aid at eligible charges.

name: Camras Scholars
value: First-year tuition amount for four undergraduate years, or five in architecture; the fixed award does not cover tuition increases. Full-time enrollment is required. Program-specific academic renewal criteria are not published.
deadline: November 15 Early Action/Early Decision application; late December finalist notice and February roundtable interview (years unstated). Fall 2027 dates are unconfirmed.
apply: Submit the completed Early Action or Early Decision admission application, transcripts and optional test scores by November 15; no separate scholarship application. Finalists complete leadership and major-related roundtable discussions at the Leadership Symposium.
eligibility: Strong academics, extracurricular involvement and leadership; enroll in at least 12 credits each semester. The page lists U.S. citizens/permanent residents and also describes the program as Dreamer friendly; the precise Dreamer exception requires clarification.
notes: Scholars contribute through leadership, research and service. Illinois Tech institutional scholarships do not stack. Camras supports bachelor’s tuition only; accelerated master’s coursework may use the original Heald award at the undergraduate rate. Combined MAP/Camras aid cannot exceed eligible tuition and mandatory fees.

name: Wells Scholars
value: Full cost of attendance for eight undergraduate semesters, including tuition for 12-18 credits, mandatory/course fees and a standard housing/meal stipend that remains available off campus. Additional approved summer, research and study-abroad funding may be available.
deadline: IU admission by November 1 (year unstated on program pages). Domestic portal: November 2, 2026, 11:59 p.m. EST nomination/material deadline, conflicting with the domestic program page’s November 1, 5 p.m. EST rule. International nominations: November 1, 11:59 p.m. EST (year unstated). February interview dates are not confirmed for 2027.
apply: Complete IU admission and nomination materials. Domestic school nominations are preferred, with up to two nominees per school; self-nomination is available when the school has used its two slots or for qualifying alternative circumstances. International candidates follow the OIS/program nomination route. Finalists interview.
eligibility: High-school seniors, including international students. U.S. residents/passport holders use the domestic route even at schools abroad. Academic, leadership and community engagement are considered; published past-recipient GPA/test profiles are not minimum requirements and testing is optional. Binding Early Decision applicants to other institutions are ineligible.
notes: Maintain both semester and cumulative 3.4 GPA, at least 12 credits each semester and high ethical standards; first-year program seminars are required. Other campus awards cannot exceed cost of attendance. Domestic official deadline pages conflict, and international dates lack a cycle year.

name: Stamps Scholars
value: Tuition and fees plus estimated books, personal expenses and transportation for up to four full-time undergraduate years, or five for architecture/approved dual-degree programs; $12,000 enrichment fund. Housing/meals and specific academic renewal criteria are not listed.
deadline: REA November 1, 2026; RD January 4, 2027
apply: All Restrictive Early Action and Regular Decision applicants are considered automatically. Candidates receive any required follow-up instructions in early December for REA or early March for RD; no separate initial scholarship application.
eligibility: First-year admission applicants, including international students, with exceptional academics, leadership and character; recipients must remain full-time undergraduates.
notes: The listed scholarship expenses do not include housing or meals, so full cost-of-attendance coverage is not established. Follow-up deadlines and program-specific renewal criteria are not published.

name: National Alumni Scholarship
value: Multiple merit awards up to full tuition, renewable for up to four undergraduate years or until the first bachelor’s degree, whichever comes first. Specific National Alumni renewal GPA is not clearly separated from Carpenter terms.
deadline: 2027 dates not yet published (last cycle December 1, 2025)
apply: Start and complete admission, all admission checklist items and the separate National Alumni Scholarship application. Invited semifinalists complete a scholarship interview to compete for full tuition or one of three Carpenter awards.
eligibility: Enter directly from high school in summer or fall; cumulative GPA at least 3.8 on a 4.0 scale OR top 5% of the class; weighted GPAs accepted. Academic achievement, leadership, service, initiative and commitment are considered. Citizenship restrictions are not stated on the award page.
notes: Full-time enrollment (at least 12 credits) and satisfactory academic progress required. The page gives a 3.25 renewal GPA in the Carpenter section; confirm the full-tuition award’s individual GPA terms. Fall/spring tuition-specific assistance cannot exceed tuition. The page still describes the 2026 competition; 2027 rules and dates need confirmation.

name: George A. Carpenter Scholarship
value: $10,000 annually for up to four undergraduate years or until the first bachelor’s degree, whichever comes first; tuition-only and combinable with Presidential merit.
deadline: 2027 dates not yet published (last cycle December 1, 2025)
apply: Start and complete admission, all admission checklist items and the separate National Alumni Scholarship application. Invited semifinalists complete a scholarship interview to compete for full tuition or one of three Carpenter awards.
eligibility: Enter directly from high school in summer or fall; cumulative GPA at least 3.8 on a 4.0 scale OR top 5% of the class; weighted GPAs accepted. Academic achievement, leadership, service, initiative and commitment are considered. Citizenship restrictions are not stated on the award page.
notes: Maintain full-time enrollment (at least 12 credits), 3.25 GPA and satisfactory academic progress. Recipients meet Alumni & Development each semester, engage in campus leadership and participate in annual scholarship competition days. Fall/spring tuition-specific assistance cannot exceed tuition. The page still describes the 2026 competition; 2027 rules and dates need confirmation.

name: Brown Fellows (ending)
value: Program ends in 2027.
deadline: Not open for fall 2027
apply: Current alternatives: Lincoln and Grissom Scholars (tuition, fees, housing, meals, enrichment), separate premier applications due December 1 (recurring). General automatic merit $20,000-$45,000/year.
eligibility: Grissom has additional first-generation eligibility.
notes: Lincoln and Grissom should become their own listings.

name: Presidential Scholarship
value: Four-year renewable in-state or out-of-state tuition and mandatory fees.
deadline: December 1, 2026: completed admission, competitive scholarship section and all supporting documents/qualifying test scores. Apply earlier because funds may be exhausted. Scholarship acceptance encouraged by May 1, 2027; any interview date is provided by invitation.
apply: Complete admission and its competitive scholarship section and submit all required supporting documents, including transcript and any qualifying scores, by December 1, 2026. Selected applicants may be invited to interview; awards are competitive.
eligibility: 3.50 unweighted GPA plus ACT 31/SAT 1390, OR 4.00 unweighted GPA with test-optional application. Incoming first-time freshmen, Kentucky residents/nonresidents and international applicants. Scores must be from one sitting; no superscoring.
notes: Maintain at least 12 credits each semester and 3.0 cumulative GPA, checked after spring. Only one listed academic/competitive/selective award; a higher award replaces the lower one. William C. Parker may stack under its rules, but tuition scholarship recipients cannot receive Legacy Tuition funding. Scholarship enrollment normally begins in the fall after high-school graduation; deferral requires a separate appeal. No demonstrated-need requirement.

name: Otis A. Singletary Scholarship
value: Four-year renewable in-state or out-of-state tuition, mandatory/course/program fees and a housing/dining stipend for the first two years in a UK residence hall. The stipend amount is not published.
deadline: December 1, 2026: completed admission, competitive scholarship section and all supporting documents/qualifying test scores. Apply earlier because funds may be exhausted. Scholarship acceptance encouraged by May 1, 2027; any interview date is provided by invitation.
apply: Complete admission and its competitive scholarship section and submit all required supporting documents, including transcript and any qualifying scores, by December 1, 2026. Selected applicants may be invited to interview; awards are competitive.
eligibility: 3.80 unweighted GPA plus ACT 33/SAT 1450, OR 4.00 unweighted GPA with test-optional application. Incoming first-time freshmen, Kentucky residents/nonresidents and international applicants. Scores must be from one sitting; no superscoring.
notes: Maintain at least 12 credits each semester and 3.40 cumulative GPA, checked after spring. Only one listed academic/competitive/selective award; a higher award replaces the lower one. William C. Parker may stack under its rules, but tuition scholarship recipients cannot receive Legacy Tuition funding. Scholarship enrollment normally begins in the fall after high-school graduation; deferral requires a separate appeal. No demonstrated-need requirement.

name: Brown Fellows (ending)
value: Program ends in 2027.
deadline: Not open for fall 2027
apply: Louisville identifies Grawemeyer as a full-ride mentored program; its fall-2027 requirements were not established.

name: Stamps Scholarship
value: Full cost of attendance for four years, including tuition, fees, housing/meals, books and supplies; approximate annual values $33,000 Louisiana residents/$50,000 nonresidents. Potential $14,000 enrichment fund and opportunity to earn up to $1,550 annually through research participation.
deadline: December 1, 2026 priority deadline for admission, required documents and Honors writing sample. January semifinalist essay/résumé request; later campus Scholars Weekend interview dates are not confirmed for 2027.
apply: Complete Common App admission, select Honors consideration and submit required documents and the writing sample through LSU’s portal. Invited semifinalists submit an essay/résumé; finalists attend all campus Scholars Weekend activities and interview.
eligibility: Entering Ogden Honors College freshmen with outstanding academics, leadership and service. Honors pages say all Honors applicants, including international applicants, are considered; the general aid page limits international freshman consideration to students from U.S. or American schools abroad. Confirm how this restriction applies to the award.
notes: Renewal: cumulative 3.0 GPA and 24 credits annually, checked after spring; continuous fall/spring enrollment and funding availability required. Part-time withdrawal rules differ by award; consult the retention policy. No scholarship funds during probation without an approved appeal. International eligibility and 2027 Scholars Weekend dates need clarification.

name: Chancellor's Alumni Scholarship
value: Full cost of attendance for four years, including tuition, fees, housing/meals, books and supplies; approximate annual values $33,000 Louisiana residents/$50,000 nonresidents. $2,000 study-abroad stipend and opportunity to earn up to $1,550 annually through research participation.
deadline: December 1, 2026 priority deadline for admission, required documents and Honors writing sample. January semifinalist essay/résumé request; later campus Scholars Weekend interview dates are not confirmed for 2027.
apply: Complete Common App admission, select Honors consideration and submit required documents and the writing sample through LSU’s portal. Invited semifinalists submit an essay/résumé; finalists attend all campus Scholars Weekend activities and interview.
eligibility: Entering Ogden Honors College freshmen with outstanding academics, leadership and service. Honors pages say all Honors applicants, including international applicants, are considered; the general aid page limits international freshman consideration to students from U.S. or American schools abroad. Confirm how this restriction applies to the award.
notes: Renewal: cumulative 3.0 GPA and 24 credits annually, checked after spring; continuous fall/spring enrollment and funding availability required. Part-time withdrawal rules differ by award; consult the retention policy. No scholarship funds during probation without an approved appeal. The retention policy identifies President’s Alumni as the former Chancellor’s Alumni award; current Honors pages still use Chancellor’s Alumni. International eligibility and 2027 Scholars Weekend dates need clarification.

name: Dean's Honor Scholarship
value: Full tuition for four undergraduate years, or five in the accredited five-year architecture track. Maintain 3.0 cumulative GPA and continuous full-time Newcomb-Tulane College enrollment.
deadline: Admission: November 1 ED I, November 10 EA, January 15 ED II/RD. Aid priority: November 15 ED I, December 15 EA, January 15 ED II, February 15 RD (years unstated). Current merit consideration follows the admission/aid process; Fall 2027 dates are unconfirmed.
apply: Complete admission, CSS Profile, FAFSA if eligible, requested supporting documents and optional test scores for fullest merit consideration. International non-U.S. citizens also submit the Declaration & Certification of Finances. No separate initial DHS application starting with the high-school class of 2026; an optional supplement may be uploaded.
eligibility: Incoming first-time undergraduate applicants, including international students. Academic excellence, leadership and community involvement are evaluated; published recipient GPA/test profiles are not minimums. Scores are optional but preferred for scholarship review; financial information may also be evaluated.
notes: At least 12 credits each fall/spring; June renewal review and academic/student conduct requirements apply. Cannot combine DHS with another Tulane merit award, ROTC, faculty/staff waiver or Tuition Exchange; partial athletic and qualifying need-based aid may combine. Admissions confirms the newer no-separate-application rule; older DHS aid text still mentions a scholarship application. Current Stamps and Grossman & Cohen are separate awards; a new Paul Tulane award is not established.

name: Charles R. Westgate Engineering Scholarship
value: Full tuition for four years (not room and board). Up to two incoming students.
deadline: ED I admission: November 1, 2026; ED II/RD: January 2, 2027. Scholarship selection is announced with admission: December 11, 2026 ED I; February 12, 2027 ED II; March 24, 2027 RD. Enrollment replies: January 15, 2027 ED I; February 26, 2027 ED II; May 1, 2027 RD.
apply: No separate initial application.
eligibility: First-year applicants indicating an engineering major, with an outstanding high-school record, leadership, science-fair achievement or independent research. Recipients must continue in Whiting Engineering and maintain at least a 3.0 GPA.
notes: Up to two incoming scholars annually. Selection is automatic with admission, without extra scholarship materials; awards are announced through the applicant portal with admission and cannot be appealed.

name: Presidential Fellowship
value: Full tuition for four years while living on campus, or $34,000 annually for four years off campus. Fees, housing and meals are excluded.
deadline: Complete admission by November 1 (year unstated), plus fellowship application/Cornerstone Project. Finalist notice mid-November; interviews December-January; results by March 1 (years unstated). Fall 2027 project deadline is unconfirmed.
apply: Submit admission and the separate fellowship application/Cornerstone Project in an accepted electronic format. Finalists interview; submitted materials count only after the automated confirmation email. Google Drive/OneDrive project links are not accepted.
eligibility: Freshman applicants with at least 3.7 GPA on a 4.0 scale or 93/100, weighted or unweighted. International students are ineligible; the page does not define how permanent residents are categorized.
notes: Maintain 3.25 cumulative GPA, complete assigned Leadership or Service Scholars Program requirements and appropriately represent the university. Cannot combine with other Stevenson awards or defer the fellowship. The linked application system could not be read to establish current project dates.

name: Banneker/Key Scholars
value: Up to eight consecutive undergraduate semesters. Full award: tuition, standard mandatory fees, standard housing/food and book allowance, adjusted for living with parents versus on/off campus. Partial award: $8,000 annually in-state/$12,000 out-of-state plus books; published $1,250 book allowance is a 2026-2027 estimate.
deadline: November 1 Early Action admission and all required materials; invited interviews in late February/early March, invitation by March 1 and award notice by April 1 (years unstated). Fall 2027 stages are unconfirmed.
apply: Complete EA admission and receive Honors College consideration. Selected applicants interview.
eligibility: Incoming fall freshmen invited to Honors, with academic achievement/leadership. U.S. citizens and eligible noncitizens are considered under UMD’s merit policy; spring admits are excluded.
notes: At least 12 credits each semester, 3.20 cumulative GPA without rounding and 30 earned credits per academic year; precollege AP/IB credits do not count. Winter/summer coursework can restore credits/GPA but is not funded. One GPA probationary semester; no credit-completion probation. Annual merit acknowledgement required. No stacking with UMD President’s/Dean’s/transfer merit; total aid capped at attendance costs. Excludes miscellaneous, departmental, health, parking and study-abroad fees, graduate coursework and unused semesters after graduation.

name: Gabelli Presidential Scholars
value: Full tuition for four undergraduate years and fully funded program-sponsored summer experiences; approximately 18 incoming scholars. Housing is guaranteed for four years but housing/meals are not covered by the merit award.
deadline: Submit admission by November 1 regardless of ED I/ED II/RD round (year unstated). Finalist invitation/admission by February 1; funded campus evaluation in mid-February (years unstated). Fall 2027 stages are unconfirmed.
apply: Submit BC admission by the scholarship priority date; no separate scholarship application or financial-aid forms required for merit selection. Invited finalists attend the funded campus visit, interviews and other evaluations.
eligibility: Incoming first-year bachelor’s applicants, including international students; transfers excluded. Outstanding academics, leadership and service; no minimum GPA/SAT requirement.
notes: Maintain 3.6 GPA and model citizenship in the BC community. Summer experiences are funded separately. Qualifying need-based aid may supplement tuition merit; sponsored BC study abroad can retain aid. Apply by November 1 even when choosing a later admission round.

name: Presidential Scholarship (Trustee unconfirmed)
value: Presidential: half tuition annually for up to four undergraduate years, effective for students entering Fall 2026 onward. Current Trustee full-tuition offering is not established.
deadline: December 1 admission deadline
apply: Apply for admission by December 1.
eligibility: Incoming first-year students from around the world with exceptional academics and leadership; Presidential has no citizenship restriction.
notes: General merit renewal requires at least 2.0 GPA, satisfactory completion of 12 credits each semester, disciplinary good standing and any additional award-letter/merit-guide conditions. Admissions currently lists Presidential only; financial-aid pages still reference Trustee. Confirm any individual renewal requirements.

name: Presidential Scholarship
value: Full tuition, campus housing and meals for four undergraduate years; approximately five recipients. General institutional-aid satisfactory progress applies; specific Presidential renewal criteria are not published.
deadline: Admission: November 1 ED I/EA; January 15 ED II/RD (years unstated). Selected finalists interview; Fall 2027 scholarship interview dates are unpublished.
apply: All applicants considered; no separate application. Finalists interview.
eligibility: Admitted incoming undergraduate applicants, regardless of citizenship, with exceptional academics and leadership. Merit selection does not consider financial need and test scores do not affect merit decisions.
notes: General institutional-aid progress requires 2.0 cumulative GPA and 67% completion of attempted credits; Clark-funded aid ordinarily ends after eight semesters. Confirm any additional Presidential renewal terms. International applicants submit certification of finances; admission is need-aware, and expenses beyond tuition/housing/meals remain the student’s responsibility.

name: First-year merit (University Scholars unconfirmed)
value: First-year merit amounts vary; individual award values are not published. Merit ordinarily supports up to eight in-class undergraduate semesters, subject to the scholarship contract. The historical full-tuition University Scholars award is not confirmed.
deadline: First-year merit consideration requires admission application by January 1 Regular Decision deadline (year unstated). Fall 2027 award-specific dates are unconfirmed.
apply: Automatic consideration with admission.
eligibility: First-year admission applicants with exceptional academics and achievements, including international applicants. General merit has no separate initial application; some named awards have additional requirements.
notes: Maintain full-time program enrollment, quantitative satisfactory academic progress and the GPA/service requirements in the individual merit contract. GPA shortfall allows one funded probationary semester. Current pages separately list a Stamps full-attendance-cost scholarship with an invited video application and mid-March selection; its precise award/renewal and international rules are not established here. Torch is a separate first-generation/access award, not confirmation of the old University Scholars program.

name: General merit (Foisie Scholars unconfirmed)
value: General merit varies and renews for four years, up to 16 terms or completion of the undergraduate degree. Early Decision admits from Fall 2026 onward receive at least $25,000 annually; historical Foisie full-tuition terms are unconfirmed.
deadline: Admission: November 1 ED I/EA I; January 5 ED II/EA II; February 1 RD (years unstated). Fall 2027 dates are not explicitly confirmed.
apply: Automatic consideration with admission.
eligibility: First-year applicants automatically considered based on academics, recommendations, leadership, activities and service; international applicants can receive merit. Recipients of WPI employee tuition benefits cannot receive academic merit.
notes: Remain full-time with at least 12 credits per semester, good academic standing and at least 24 passed credits in A-D terms annually; awards decrease 5% for each three-credit shortfall beginning at 21 credits. AP/transfer/incomplete credits do not count. Scholarship amounts do not increase with tuition, are tuition-capped and ordinarily exclude summer. Early Decision minimum cannot combine with Innovation Award. Historical 2014 Foisie gift supported students with financial need but does not establish a current named full-tuition award.

name: Alumni Distinguished Scholarship
value: Full tuition for up to 18 credits each semester, matching fees, double-occupancy MSU housing, DineOn Silver meals and $1000 annually, for eight consecutive undergraduate fall/spring semesters; renewal requires 3.2 GPA, at least 12 credits each semester and Honors College membership.
deadline: Admission by November 1 (year unstated) for invitation to the scholarship competition. Fall 2027 examination, essay/interview and selection dates are not published.
apply: Apply for admission by the priority date; outstanding applicants are invited to the competition and examination. The official 2026 cohort description also included short essays and selection interviews; current invited instructions control.
eligibility: Outstanding incoming first-year applicants selected by academic/intellectual performance and competition participation; recipients must remain in MSU Honors College while pursuing their first undergraduate MSU degree.
notes: Complete at least 12 credits each semester and maintain 3.2 cumulative GPA. One GPA probationary semester; ineligible semesters count toward the eight-semester maximum. Initial award cannot be deferred, and later enrollment interruption requires an approved leave. MSU may adjust for other awards; need-based aid may decrease. Annual ADS/UDS cohort participation is expected. Distinct from National Merit.

name: Distinguished First-year Scholarship
value: Tuition for up to 18 credits each semester and matching fees for eight consecutive fall/spring undergraduate semesters; 20 Alumni Distinguished competition runners-up.
deadline: Admission by November 1 (year unstated) for invitation to the scholarship competition. Fall 2027 examination, essay/interview and selection dates are not published.
apply: Apply for admission by the priority date; outstanding applicants are invited to the competition and examination. The official 2026 cohort description also included short essays and selection interviews; current invited instructions control.
eligibility: Outstanding incoming first-year applicants selected by academic/intellectual performance and competition participation; recipients must remain in MSU Honors College while pursuing their first undergraduate MSU degree.
notes: Complete at least 12 credits each semester and maintain 3.2 cumulative GPA. One GPA probationary semester; ineligible semesters count toward the eight-semester maximum. Initial award cannot be deferred, and later enrollment interruption requires an approved leave. MSU may adjust for other awards; need-based aid may decrease. Distinct from National Merit.

name: Presidential Endowed Scholarship Package
value: Tuition, campus housing at assigned double-occupancy rate and meal plan for up to four undergraduate years/eight semesters; $12,000 enrichment usable after the first year. Nonresidents may also receive full nonresident tuition coverage.
deadline: General Scholarship Application opens October 1, 2026; December 1, 2026 scholarship priority and qualifying test-score deadline. The separate Presidential application has its own portal deadline, not publicly specified.
apply: Gain admission, complete the General Scholarship Application and the separate Presidential Endowed application in the portal, including required essays. Join Shackouls Honors; selection includes an interview.
eligibility: Entering first-time freshmen, Shackouls Honors members, grades 9-11 GPA at least 3.75 plus ACT 30 or SAT 1360. The current award page is tagged Fall 2027, Mississippi/nonresident and international.
notes: Maintain at least 3.4 overall college GPA and continuous enrollment of at least 12 credits each semester. Housing support requires continuous campus residency. Package replaces other freshman academic, national-recognition and National Merit packages; total aid cannot exceed attendance costs.

name: Stamps Scholarship
value: Up to full cost of attendance after other awards, plus a $12,000 enrichment fund for approved educational activities. Current Stamps-specific duration and academic renewal thresholds are not published on the award pages.
deadline: January 10 (recurring; year not specified)
apply: Apply for admission, then complete the separate Freshman Scholarship Application. International candidates should contact the global office for review for nomination by the Senior International Officer.
eligibility: First-time freshmen entering Ole Miss in fall with exceptional academics and leadership. International candidates are eligible through the nomination route; no hard admission test/GPA cutoff is specified for Stamps.
notes: Other awards are coordinated within the attendance-cost package. The international page confirms Stamps full attendance costs and enrichment; its generic four-year international merit renewal text is not clearly assigned to Stamps. Confirm the award-specific renewal contract.

name: Presidential Scholarship
value: Full tuition, campus room and board at double-occupancy residence-hall rate. Award-specific maximum duration and renewal GPA requirements are not clearly published.
deadline: December 1 priority application date (recurring)
apply: Apply for admission as a first-time, full-time on-campus freshman for fall entry. Selected candidates who meet the minimum criteria are invited to University Scholars Weekend competition and interview.
eligibility: First-time, full-time on-campus fall freshmen with cumulative GPA at least 3.75 on a 4.0 scale OR ACT 27/SAT 1290; writing scores excluded. GPA weighting and a scholarship-specific citizenship restriction are not stated.
notes: The ten-consecutive-semester footnote is placed under automatic scholarships and cannot safely establish the competitive award duration. Obtain the award renewal contract.

name: Trustee Scholarship
value: Full tuition. Award-specific maximum duration and renewal GPA requirements are not clearly published.
deadline: December 1 priority application date (recurring)
apply: Apply for admission as a first-time, full-time on-campus freshman for fall entry. Selected candidates who meet the minimum criteria are invited to University Scholars Weekend competition and interview.
eligibility: First-time, full-time on-campus fall freshmen with cumulative GPA at least 3.75 on a 4.0 scale OR ACT 27/SAT 1290; writing scores excluded. GPA weighting and a scholarship-specific citizenship restriction are not stated.
notes: The ten-consecutive-semester footnote is placed under automatic scholarships and cannot safely establish the competitive award duration. Obtain the award renewal contract.

name: Presidential Scholarship
value: The current award amount and covered costs are not published on the scholarship/application pages. Institutional renewal is limited to five academic years or the first bachelor’s degree, whichever comes first.
deadline: Official pages conflict: scholarship application says November 15 without a cycle year; admission calendar for the Fall 2027 class says December 1. The application page still requests a 2026-27 FAFSA, so Fall 2027 requirements need confirmation.
apply: Gain admission, send a sixth-semester transcript and ACT/SAT scores, and complete the separate scholarship application in one sitting with academic details, activities/achievements and a video about interests, goals and career plans. FAFSA required on the application page, but its listed year is outdated for Fall 2027.
eligibility: At least 3.90 cumulative GPA through junior year. The first-year scholarship page requires ACT31/SAT1390 while the application page says ACT30/SAT1370. Qualifying tests through October of senior year; highest composite or superscore used. No GPA weighting or precise citizenship eligibility is stated.
notes: For awards from Summer 2026 onward, renewal requires 2.75 cumulative GPA and 30 completed credits per year, reviewed after spring; summer can remedy deficiencies and other-institution/dual credits can count. Confirm the amount, score threshold, FAFSA cycle and conflicting deadline before applying.

name: Presidential Scholarship
value: Full tuition for up to 18 credits per semester over ten consecutive full-time fall/spring undergraduate semesters. The page also calls it a four-year award; confirm the extension in the award letter.
deadline: December 1 (recurring)
apply: Submit freshman admission and all required materials, then the separate Presidential application in Billiken Gateway with a 500-word leadership essay, resume and two recommendations. Invited candidates interview; the prior admitted-student process used a recorded StandOut interview and required campus/admitted-student visit, with counselor alternatives.
eligibility: Incoming first-year applicants, including international students at the St. Louis campus; at least 3.85 cumulative high-school GPA weighted or unweighted on the junior-year transcript. SAT/ACT not required; international English proficiency rules still apply.
notes: Replaces other SLU merit awards. Presidential Scholars may request up to $1,200 for an investigative learning experience. Scholarship-specific renewal GPA is not provided on current award/catalog pages. The interview page is still the 2026 admitted-student cycle; 2027 dates/process need confirmation.

name: Danforth Scholars
value: Full tuition with a $2,500 stipend or partial/half tuition. Renews annually for the degree program while maintaining academic progress and the program’s character/participation standards. Tuition awards do not cover housing.
deadline: Admission priority December 16, 2026; separate Pathway scholarship response January 4, 2027. Finalists notified by end of February 2027; required virtual events/interview in early March 2027, with exact dates sent to finalists. Awards announced in March 2027.
apply: Submit Common or Coalition admission application, then the individual 250-word scholar response in WashU Pathway. Counselor and teacher admission recommendations are reviewed; a third community/leadership recommendation is optional and encouraged. Finalists must attend the virtual events and interview to remain eligible.
eligibility: Incoming first-year applicants to any undergraduate school, including international applicants; transfers excluded. Demonstrated leadership through service, community commitment, academic excellence and personal integrity. No numerical GPA/test floor is published.
notes: May apply to more than one Signature Scholar program. Early Decision commitments precede scholarship decisions. Scholars participate in program/community activities; approved WashU academic-year study abroad can be funded. Need aid is coordinated with merit.

name: Annika Rodriguez Scholars
value: Full tuition with a $2,500 stipend or partial/half tuition. Renews annually for the degree program while maintaining academic progress and the program’s character/participation standards. Tuition awards do not cover housing.
deadline: Admission priority December 16, 2026; separate Pathway scholarship response January 4, 2027. Finalists notified by end of February 2027; required virtual events/interview in early March 2027, with exact dates sent to finalists. Awards announced in March 2027.
apply: Submit Common or Coalition admission application, then the individual 250-word scholar response in WashU Pathway. Counselor and teacher admission recommendations are reviewed; a third community/leadership recommendation is optional and encouraged. Finalists must attend the virtual events and interview to remain eligible.
eligibility: Incoming first-year applicants to any undergraduate school, including international applicants; transfers excluded. Academic and leadership achievements, community service and bringing diverse groups together. No numerical GPA/test floor is published.
notes: May apply to more than one Signature Scholar program. Early Decision commitments precede scholarship decisions. Scholars participate in program/community activities; approved WashU academic-year study abroad can be funded. Need aid is coordinated with merit.

name: John B. Ervin Scholars
value: Full tuition with a $2,500 stipend or partial/half tuition. Renews annually for the degree program while maintaining academic progress and the program’s character/participation standards. Tuition awards do not cover housing.
deadline: Admission priority December 16, 2026; separate Pathway scholarship response January 4, 2027. Finalists notified by end of February 2027; required virtual events/interview in early March 2027, with exact dates sent to finalists. Awards announced in March 2027.
apply: Submit Common or Coalition admission application, then the individual 250-word scholar response in WashU Pathway. Counselor and teacher admission recommendations are reviewed; a third community/leadership recommendation is optional and encouraged. Finalists must attend the virtual events and interview to remain eligible.
eligibility: Incoming first-year applicants to any undergraduate school who are U.S. citizens, permanent residents, or undocumented/DACA students living in the U.S.; transfers excluded. Academic excellence, leadership, community service and commitment to diversity/social justice. No numerical GPA/test floor is published.
notes: May apply to more than one Signature Scholar program. Early Decision commitments precede scholarship decisions. Scholars participate in program/community activities; approved WashU academic-year study abroad can be funded. Need aid is coordinated with merit.

name: Presidential Scholarship
value: Four-year merit scholarship with a fixed award amount that does not rise with tuition or inflation; current dollars and food/housing allowance amount are not publicly specified. Presidential Scholars receive an initial two-year campus-housing arrangement and optional guaranteed on-campus housing for all four years.
deadline: Fall 2027 admission: November 1, 2026 Early Action or December 1, 2026 Regular Decision. Apply by December 1, 2026 with Honors College consideration for merit. Admission acceptance by May 1, 2027 accepts the merit offer; scholarship notifications begin in early March.
apply: Apply to Rutgers–New Brunswick by December 1, choose Honors College consideration and complete the additional Honors College essay, which also serves as the merit essay. No separate scholarship application. Honors admission and award are based on the first-choice academic school.
eligibility: Competitive entering first-year Honors College applicants at Rutgers–New Brunswick. Award amounts vary with in-state, out-of-state, international and need status. Selection considers academics, the applicant pool and available funds; no numerical high-school GPA/test floor published and test-optional applicants receive consideration.
notes: Renew with at least 12 degree credits each semester, 24 degree credits completed by spring’s end annually and at least 3.5 GPA; summer credits do not count. First-year Honors College participation/residence required; second-year university-owned housing. Students who lived on campus and received the first-two-year food/housing allowance may use it on or off campus in years three/four. Awards are attendance-cost capped and residence changes can alter amounts. Newark BA/MD Presidential is a separate medical-program award.

name: Presidential Academic Scholarship
value: Full tuition, for up to eight fall/spring semesters or 120 credits; full-time enrollment, good standing and satisfactory academic progress required.
deadline: General admission is rolling; no Presidential-specific Fall 2027 priority date is published. The catalog gives international fall admission an August 1 deadline without a cycle year.
apply: Apply for freshman admission; awards are decided at admission by holistic Admissions Committee review. Test-optional applicants must submit an additional essay of at least 500 words with the transcript and recommendation. Presidential candidates receive additional review and may be asked for further documents.
eligibility: Incoming undergraduate freshmen evaluated by the Admissions Committee without a published Presidential GPA/test floor. Test-optional applicants receive consideration with extra review. A Presidential-specific citizenship restriction is not stated.
notes: Scholarships cannot stack or combine with tuition waivers/exchange awards, and total gift aid is capped at direct costs. Study abroad is excluded except ISEP tuition exchange. SAP depends on attempted credits: cumulative GPA minimum rises from 1.5 at 24-47 credits to 2.0 at 96+; completion-rate standards and 150% maximum attempted-credit limit also apply.

name: Ann P. Neupauer Scholarship
value: Full tuition for up to eight semesters.
deadline: Admission: November 15 ED I; December 1 Early Action; January 5 ED II/Regular Decision (years unstated). No separate Neupauer application deadline; Fall 2027 admission cycle dates are not explicitly confirmed.
apply: Apply for undergraduate admission on time; automatically considered without a separate Neupauer application. CSS Profile is required for institutional need-based aid and FAFSA for federal/state aid, rather than a separately stated Neupauer merit application.
eligibility: Undergraduates studying engineering, mathematics or computer science, selected for exceptional academics; no numerical high-school GPA/test floor or Neupauer-specific citizenship restriction is published. Second bachelor’s degree applicants are not eligible for Stevens merit.
notes: Renew for up to eight full-time undergraduate semesters with at least 3.2 GPA and satisfactory academic progress; merit awards cannot exceed tuition. If donor-funded, recipients are expected to thank their donor.

name: Regents Scholarship
value: For 2027-28, approximately $15,500 per year for New Mexico residents or $24,000 for nonresidents, covering base tuition, fees and housing; nonresidents also receive a waiver to resident tuition rates. Four years/eight consecutive fall-spring undergraduate semesters, about 12 new awards annually. Additional board/books coverage described on the undated program site is not itemized in the 2027-28 table.
deadline: Complete admission and the separate Regents application by December 1, 2026 for 2027-28. Selection/acceptance dates are not confirmed for this cycle; the latest linked August 2024 handbook used January 31 offers and May 1 acceptance.
apply: Gain admission and complete the separate Regents application linked through the UNM Scholarship Office/AwardSpring. The program’s application page confirms essay questions and a video. The latest linked 2024 handbook specifies activities/awards, three 350-word essays and a video of at most two minutes; confirm current portal instructions.
eligibility: Incoming freshmen, New Mexico residents and nonresidents, with at least 3.90 unweighted cumulative high-school GPA; the table also lists a GED scaled score of 175 or higher. No Regents-specific citizenship restriction is stated. Maintain 15 new credit hours and at least 3.3 GPA each fall/spring semester.
notes: Freshmen must live in Scholars Wing, Hokona Hall, with documented exceptions. Main-campus credit rules apply; AP/CLEP/concurrent credits and failed/audited courses do not meet renewal requirements. First bachelor’s completion ends eligibility and ineligible semesters count toward eight; approved leave/co-op can pause funding. The latest linked 2024 handbook adds Honors degree/certificate progress, an annual report and increasing service/leadership requirements, but the entering-year handbook governs and a 2027 version is unpublished.

name: Presidential Scholarship
value: New York residents: $15,000 annually. International/nonresident students: up to $22,000 annually. Renew for four undergraduate years/eight semesters; coordinated with other aid within attendance costs.
deadline: Presidential application January 4, 2027 for Fall 2027 admission. General admission scholarship priority is November 1 without an explicit year; Presidential offers must be accepted through the Honors portal by May 1 before fall entry.
apply: Submit UB admission application, then use the emailed applicant-status login to complete the separate Presidential application. Accept the award in the Honors College online portal. Recipients take the one-credit HON 101 Presidential seminar in their first semester.
eligibility: Top entering first-year students, including international and out-of-state students. No minimum high-school GPA/test criteria; SAT/ACT optional. Published 2024 class GPA ranges describe recipients, not thresholds.
notes: Remain Honors College enrolled, at least 12 credits each semester and complete 24 credits annually. Overall UB GPA at least 3.30 in the first year, then 3.50 in later years; reviewed after spring, with summer grades applied to the next review and only UB courses included. GPA failure ends the award unless an appeal is approved. Approved leave may preserve eligibility; residence changes can adjust the amount.

name: Presidential Scholarship
value: Domestic award: tuition and fees after other tuition aid, campus double-room/meal costs and up to $20,000 enrichment across four years. International award page: full tuition and campus double-room costs, excluding fees and meals; enrichment is not listed. Maximum eight fall/spring undergraduate semesters.
deadline: Fall 2027 admission: EA/ED I November 1, 2026; ED II/RD January 3, 2027. Completion deadlines November 20, 2026 or January 20, 2027. Domestic FAFSA/CSS: November 15, 2026 EA/ED I; January 15, 2027 ED II; February 1, 2027 RD. International CSS: November 1, 2026 early or January 3, 2027 later rounds.
apply: Admission application also serves as scholarship application. Submit applicable FAFSA/CSS documents by the admission-plan financial-aid deadline; domestic merit disbursement and renewal require FAFSA. International students follow the separate international aid rules.
eligibility: Entering traditional first-year full-time undergraduates with exceptional academics and personal qualities. Top 1-2% class rank is a typical profile, not a hard floor; test optional. Domestic awards require U.S. citizenship or eligible-noncitizen status; international Presidential awards are listed separately.
notes: Renew full-time with satisfactory academic progress, at least 3.0 cumulative GPA and compliance with University policies; domestic recipients also file FAFSA annually. Other tuition aid reduces the award; only half of other non-tuition external awards offsets it. Campus room support is capped at average double-room or actual lower charges. International enrichment availability is not specified.

name: Trustee Scholars
value: Full tuition for four years/eight consecutive full-time undergraduate semesters; tuition-only awards cannot cover fees, housing or specified off-campus costs.
deadline: Recommended: EA I November 15 or EA II December 15
apply: Apply for first-year admission; no separate scholarship application. Early Action is recommended for Trustee consideration.
eligibility: First-year students with exceptional academics, community/school involvement and talents. International students and second-bachelor’s applicants are ineligible. Fall 2024 recipient averages are descriptive, not minimum GPA/test requirements.
notes: General scholarship renewal requires full-time enrollment of at least 12 credits per semester, at least 24 completed annually with 18 graded credits other than P, and at least 2.8 cumulative Hofstra GPA after the first two consecutive semesters. Follow the individual scholarship letter and conduct code. Tuition aid is capped at tuition; outside awards can trigger adjustment above tuition/room/board costs. Unused semesters are forfeited.

name: Trustee Scholarship
value: Full tuition, with merit ordinarily fixed annually for four years/eight semesters. The financial-aid booklet lists 3.0 cumulative GPA renewal for Trustee after a four-semester grace period, but it describes 2025-26 and current entrant terms need confirmation.
deadline: Follow your admission round
apply: Apply for first-year admission; Admissions selects semifinalists for a late-winter Zoom interview. This competitive award requires invited steps and is not automatically awarded.
eligibility: Top first-year applicants based on academic excellence, character and leadership. No numerical entry GPA/test floor is stated; scholarship-specific nationality restrictions are not published here.
notes: Maintain full-time enrollment; the latest financial-aid booklet lists no scholarship stacking and a maximum of eight terms. The separate $1,000 annual Visit Award requires an official campus visit before the relevant admission deadline. Current Trustee-specific renewal for 2027 entrants is not explicitly dated.

name: Vilas Business & Finance Scholarship
value: Up to $50,000 annually/$200,000 over four years. Vilas-specific renewal GPA and credit requirements are not published on its program page.
deadline: January 4, 2027 consideration deadline, even for RD applicants
apply: First-year domestic applicants must indicate Vilas interest in the Common Application or St. Lawrence Application and apply by January 4. An additional 250-500-word essay or resume through the Specialty Scholarship form is optional. About 25 semifinalists interview virtually in late January; about eight finalists visit New York City for alumni interviews in early March; two or three awards typically follow.
eligibility: Domestic first-year applicants interested in a career in business, finance or related fields. A business or finance major is not required; international students are ineligible. No entry GPA/test floor is specified.
notes: The Vilas program includes an annual career/networking trip. Scholarship stacking is not permitted; the highest-value merit/specialty award is used. Confirm Vilas-specific renewal terms in the award contract.

name: Coronat Scholars
value: Full tuition for four undergraduate years, or five in an approved five-year program. Also covers one Syracuse Abroad experience; one additional summer study/research/service award is competitive. Extra demonstrated-need support requires federal-aid eligibility and both FAFSA and CSS Profile.
deadline: Apply through the selected admission plan; no separate or preferred initial Coronat deadline. Fall 2027 Early Action admission is November 1, 2026; general ED I November 1 and ED II/RD January 5 dates otherwise lack explicit years. Coronat invitations are described for January and interviews early spring without confirmed 2027 dates.
apply: All first-year Arts and Sciences/Maxwell applicants are initially considered through Common or Coalition admission. About 200 are invited by email to submit an additional written application; about 40 then interview by Zoom. Follow the invitation’s materials deadline.
eligibility: First-year applicants whose home college is Arts and Sciences or Maxwell, with exceptional academics, leadership and service. No numerical entry GPA/test floor; recipient score/GPA averages are profiles. Renew with full-time enrollment and 3.0 cumulative GPA for entrants from Fall 2026 onward (2.75 applies only to earlier entrants).
notes: A&S/Maxwell must remain the home college, including a base major there for an integrated learning major. Other-college additional majors are allowed, but transferring home college ends the award. Coronat recipients enter Renée Crown Honors; summer funding requires an additional competitive request. The federal-aid nationality condition governs extra need support rather than the tuition merit award.

name: General merit (Renaissance & Global unconfirmed)
value: Current Meliora merit listing advertises $10,000-$35,000, with an average of $20,000; the range’s payment frequency is not stated there. Merit awards stay fixed and renew for up to three additional years if minimum criteria are met. Historical Renaissance and Global full-tuition terms are not confirmed.
deadline: Highest merit consideration: all admission materials by December 1. ED I November 1; ED II/RD January 5. These deadlines have no explicit cycle year, so Fall 2027 dates are unconfirmed.
apply: All admitted undergraduate first-year and transfer applicants are considered for merit through holistic admission review. Apply through the admission plan and meet the priority materials date; specialized scholarships may require their own application or nomination.
eligibility: Outstanding academic achievement and potential, regardless of financial need. Full-time enrollment (at least 12 credits) and satisfactory academic performance are required to renew. No general merit entry GPA/test floor is published.
notes: Only one University merit scholarship per student. Current handbook says fixed awards renew up to three more years; overall aid ordinarily ends after eight semesters/first bachelor’s completion, with separate dual-degree/appeal rules. The 2016 official alumni article confirms a historical Renaissance and Global recipient, not a current award. Award-specific renewal criteria should be confirmed in the offer.
